thread:
Maya: Heads up — onboarding Nuvox13b (v1.0.3-int4) on canary cluster, seeing intermittent OOMs during scale from batch=8 -> 16. Attaching logs and quick notes.
Jorge: Saw those logs, looks like slab allocator fragmentation + lots of tiny frees. Are these prefetched KV runs or no-prefetch?
Maya: Prefetch + small-slot KV. Default model profile used: max_new_tokens=1024, batch_default=16, slot_reserve=1. OOMs concentrated when input_seq_len > 350 and concurrent inflight >12.
Priya: Can you paste the failure snippet?
Maya: ```
AllocError: OutOfMemory: slab exhausted (alloc 24MB)
  at runtime::slab::alloc (/srv/runtime/slab.cpp:482)
metrics: slab_free=1.2MB slab_used=237MB fragment_ratio=0.73
context: prefetch=true kv_slots=128 small_allocs=high
```
Ashwin: fragment_ratio ~0.73 is bad. We saw similar on Halcyon where lots of 8-64B allocations caused the slab free-list to scatter. Two quick levers: enable slab_compaction_interval (background GC) and reduce smallalloc churn (slot_reserve or batching).
Jorge: Short-term patch: lower default max_new_tokens -> 512 for Nuvox13b canary and reduce batch_default to 8. Also consider kv_soft_evict=true so session KV gets reclaimed earlier.
Priya: Agree. Also add a short-run that disables prefetch for a subset to compare memory churn.
Maya: Pushing canary update now: max_new_tokens=512, batch_default=8, slot_reserve=2, kv_soft_evict=true. Disabling aggressive prefetch on 10% of canary.
deploy-bot: canary deployment queued: nuvox13b/canary -> pool-x3 (id: dpl-7975)
Maya: Ran 2k synthetic requests load test. OOM rate dropped from 0.8% -> 0.02% on patched canary. p95 latency increased ~40ms.
Ashwin: That's an expected cost/latency tradeoff. Can you capture token cost delta? Prefetch off should reduce token volume but increasing reroutes may add latency.
Maya: Quick numbers: token/req down 6% with prefetch disabled sample; overall CPU/GPU cycles steady; cost per 1k requests +3% due to p95 tail.
Priya: Quality check: golden eval on long-form summarization (prompt set L) shows 0.6% BLEU drop when truncation hits (max_new=512). But if we enable streaming + prompt-split, quality delta is within noise (+0.1%).
Jorge: Proposal: keep conservative defaults for canary (512/batch8) and implement fallback routing for requests that indicate expected generation >512 (heuristic: user_prompt_token_estimate > 400). Fallback target: nuvox-large or dedicated pool with higher defaults.
Ashwin: Alternatively, implement memfrag gating: if fragment_ratio > 0.6 on host, temporarily lower max_new_tokens to 256 for new sessions or reroute. We already have memfrag meters in runtime. Gate decision cost is negligible.
Priya: Memfrag-gating will avoid blanket lowering and preserve quality for low-frag nodes. Worth prototyping.
Maya: Logged follow-ups: T-1234 reduce Nuvox13b canary defaults; T-1235 A/B disable prefetch for stability baseline; T-1236 implement slab_compaction param in model profile; T-1237 memfrag gating prototype.
Jorge: Also add an observability tag: nuvox13b.slab_fragment_ratio to model-level metrics so we can alert before OOM spike.
Maya: Done — dashboard panel added. Early alert threshold at 0.6, severity P2.
Priya: For rollout plan: keep canary patched for 48h, collect p50/p95/p99 latency, OOM rate, token-cost, and quality eval snapshots. If OOM < 0.05% and quality within +/-0.5% on eval, proceed to staggered rollout.
Ashwin: One more nit: check allocator page-size alignment for int4 kernels; small misaligned allocations increased fragmentation for us before — might be a kernel ABI thing.
Maya: Noted; adding to T-1236.
Jorge: Sounds good. Thanks Maya — ping when 24h numbers are in. :thumbsup:
